subject: math
title: Coordinates and Transformations: Translations, Reflections and Rotations on a Grid
seo_title: Grade 5 Coordinates and Transformations Worksheets: Translations, Reflections, Rotations (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Describe and perform translations, reflections, and rotations up to 180° on a grid, and predict the results of these transformations
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on coordinates and transformations for the Ontario curriculum: read and plot points in the first quadrant, translate points and shapes, reflect them in a line and rotate them 90° and 180° about a vertex. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: A translation slides, a reflection flips, a rotation turns. The shape never changes size.
key_sub: In (x, y), go across first, then up. In a translation every vertex moves the same way. In a reflection each vertex stays the same distance from the line. In a rotation the centre does not move.
body_html:
Reading and plotting points

A point on a grid is named by two numbers, called coordinates: (x, y). Start at the origin, (0, 0). The first number, x, tells you how far to go across. The second number, y, tells you how far to go up.

Example

A point is 2 units right of the origin and 6 units up. Name it.

Across first: x = 2. Then up: y = 6.

Answer: (2, 6)

Translations: slide the shape

A translation slides a shape left or right and up or down. It does not turn or flip. Every vertex moves the same number of units in the same direction.

MoveWhat changesExample from (5, 4)
right 2x gets bigger(7, 4)
left 2x gets smaller(3, 4)
up 2y gets bigger(5, 6)
down 2y gets smaller(5, 2)
Example

Describe the translation from (2, 7) to (8, 3).

Across: 2 to 8 is 6 units right. Up and down: 7 to 3 is 4 units down.

Answer: 6 units right and 4 units down

Reflections: flip over a line

A reflection flips a shape over a line of reflection. The image is a mirror image. Each vertex ends up the same distance from the line, on the other side.

The line x = 5 goes straight up through 5 on the x-axis. The line y = 4 goes straight across through 4 on the y-axis.

Example

Reflect (3, 4) in the line x = 5.

(3, 4) is 2 units left of the line. Go 2 units right of the line: 5 + 2 = 7. y stays 4.

Answer: (7, 4)

Rotations: turn about a point

A rotation turns a shape about a point called the centre of rotation. In Grade 5 the centre is often a vertex of the shape. The centre does not move. Say how far (90° is a quarter turn, 180° is a half turn) and which way: clockwise (the way clock hands move) or counterclockwise.

To rotate a point, describe it from the centre, then turn each direction.

Turnright becomesup becomes
90° clockwisedownright
90° counterclockwiseupleft
180° (either way)leftdown
Example

Rotate (6, 4) 90° counterclockwise about (3, 4).

(6, 4) is 3 right of the centre. In a quarter turn counterclockwise, right turns into up. So the image is 3 up from (3, 4).

Answer: (3, 7)

What stays the same

After a translation, a reflection or a rotation, the shape is in a new place, but it is the same shape and size. The side lengths, the angles and the area all stay the same.

TranslationReflectionRotation
What happensslidesflips over a lineturns about a point
Which way it facesthe same waymirror imageturned
Size and anglesthe samethe samethe same

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Swapping x and y: plotting (2, 5) at (5, 2)Go across first (x), then up (y)
Counting grid lines, starting with 1 on the start lineCount the spaces you jump
Adding for “left” or “down”Left and down make the number smaller
Stopping on the line of reflection, or going past itGo the same distance on the other side
Turning the wrong wayClockwise goes like clock hands: from 12 towards 3
Mixing up 90° and 180°90° is a quarter turn; 180° is a half turn

faq.q: What do Grade 5 students learn about transformations in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: In Grade 5 (Spatial Sense, E1.4 and E1.5), students plot and read points in the first quadrant, describe translations with coordinates, and perform reflections and rotations up to 180° on a grid, predicting where each vertex will land.

faq.q: How do you remember which coordinate comes first?
faq.a: The x-coordinate comes first: go across, then up. Many teachers say “walk before you climb”, so (2, 5) is 2 across and 5 up.

faq.q: How do you rotate a shape 90° clockwise about a vertex?
faq.a: Keep that vertex still. Describe each other vertex from it, then turn the directions a quarter turn the way clock hands move: right becomes down and up becomes right.

faq.q: What is the difference between a translation, a reflection and a rotation?
faq.a: A translation slides a shape, a reflection flips it over a line to make a mirror image, and a rotation turns it about a point. None of them changes the shape’s size or angles.

sets.title: Read and plot points in the first quadrant

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 3, then go up 5. Point A is at (3, 5). The x-coordinate (across) is written first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 6, then go up 2. Point B is at (6, 2). The x-coordinate (across) is written first. (2, 6) is point C: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point D?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 1, then go up 4. Point D is at (1, 4). The x-coordinate (across) is written first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point E?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 5, then go up 7. Point E is at (5, 7). The x-coordinate (across) is written first. (7, 5) is point F: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point G?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), do not move across, then go up 4. Point G is at (0, 4). The x-coordinate (across) is written first. A point on the y-axis has x-coordinate 0.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point H?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 7, then do not move up. Point H is at (7, 0). The x-coordinate (across) is written first. A point on the x-axis has y-coordinate 0.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point K?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 8, then go up 3. Point K is at (8, 3). The x-coordinate (across) is written first. (3, 8) is point M: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point N?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 4, then go up 9. Point N is at (4, 9). The x-coordinate (across) is written first.

items.q: What is the x-coordinate of point P?
items.e: Point P is 6 units to the right of the origin, so its x-coordinate is 6. (3 is its y-coordinate.)

items.q: What is the y-coordinate of point Q?
items.e: Point Q is 7 units up from the x-axis, so its y-coordinate is 7. (2 is its x-coordinate.)

items.q: Which point is at (4, 2)?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 4, then go up 2: that is point C. Point A is at (2, 4): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (1, 6)?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 1, then go up 6: that is point A. Point B is at (6, 1): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (5, 3)?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 5, then go up 3: that is point B. Point A is at (3, 5): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (0, 5)?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), do not move across, then go up 5: that is point D. Point A is at (5, 0): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (7, 4)?
items.e: Start at the origin (0, 0), go right 7, then go up 4: that is point B. Point A is at (4, 7): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: To plot the point (6, 3), what do you do first from the origin?
items.e: The first number, 6, is the x-coordinate. It tells you how far to go across, so go right 6. Then go up 3.

items.q: Mateo plots the point (2, 5). He starts at the origin, goes up 2, then right 5. What mistake did he make?
c: He counted the grid lines, not the spaces
items.e: In (2, 5), x = 2 comes first: go right 2, then up 5. Mateo went up 2 and right 5, so he plotted (5, 2).

items.q: Lucas starts at the origin. He walks 5 units right and 2 units up. Which coordinates name his position?
items.e: Right 5 gives x = 5. Up 2 gives y = 2. Write x first: (5, 2).

items.q: A point is on the x-axis, 8 units to the right of the origin. What are its coordinates?
items.e: 8 units right gives x = 8. The point is on the x-axis, so it does not go up: y = 0. The point is (8, 0).

items.q: On a map of a park, the playground is at (4, 1) and the pond is at (4, 6). How many units apart are they?
items.e: The x-coordinates are the same, so the pond is straight up from the playground. Up from 1 to 6 is 6 − 1 = 5 units. (6 comes from counting the grid lines.)

items.q: Point A is at (3, 4). It is translated 2 units right. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Right 2 changes x: 3 + 2 = 5. y stays 4. The new point is (5, 4).

items.q: Point A is at (6, 7). It is translated 4 units down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: x stays 6. Down 4 changes y: 7 − 4 = 3. The new point is (6, 3).

items.q: Point A is at (2, 2). It is translated 5 units right and 3 units up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Right 5 changes x: 2 + 5 = 7. Up 3 changes y: 2 + 3 = 5. The new point is (7, 5).

items.q: Point A is at (8, 3). It is translated 6 units left and 2 units up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 6 changes x: 8 − 6 = 2. Up 2 changes y: 3 + 2 = 5. The new point is (2, 5).

items.q: Point A is at (5, 9). It is translated 3 units left and 6 units down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 3 changes x: 5 − 3 = 2. Down 6 changes y: 9 − 6 = 3. The new point is (2, 3).

items.q: Point A is at (1, 6). It is translated 7 units right and 5 units down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Right 7 changes x: 1 + 7 = 8. Down 5 changes y: 6 − 5 = 1. The new point is (8, 1).

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (2, 3) and B is at (5, 1). Across: 2 to 5 is 3 units right. Up and down: 3 to 1 is 2 units down. Count the spaces you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (6, 2) and B is at (3, 6). Across: 6 to 3 is 3 units left. Up and down: 2 to 6 is 4 units up. Count the spaces you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (1, 1) and B is at (7, 4). Across: 1 to 7 is 6 units right. Up and down: 1 to 4 is 3 units up. Count the spaces you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: Point P is translated 4 units right and 3 units down. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Right 4 changes x: 2 + 4 = 6. Down 3 changes y: 6 − 3 = 3. The new point is (6, 3). That is point B.

items.q: Point P is translated 5 units left and 4 units up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Left 5 changes x: 7 − 5 = 2. Up 4 changes y: 2 + 4 = 6. The new point is (2, 6). That is point C.

items.q: Point P is translated 6 units right and 5 units up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Right 6 changes x: 1 + 6 = 7. Up 5 changes y: 1 + 5 = 6. The new point is (7, 6). That is point A.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one vertex. The vertex of A at (1, 5) moves to (6, 1) in B. That is 5 units right and 4 units down. Every vertex moves the same way.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one vertex. The vertex of A at (6, 5) moves to (1, 1) in B. That is 5 units left and 4 units down. Every vertex moves the same way.

items.q: A triangle has vertices at (1, 2), (4, 2) and (1, 6). It is translated 5 units right and 1 unit up. What are the new coordinates of the vertex at (4, 2)?
items.e: Right 5 changes x: 4 + 5 = 9. Up 1 changes y: 2 + 1 = 3. The new point is (9, 3). Every vertex moves the same way.

items.q: A rectangle has vertices at (3, 5), (8, 5), (8, 9) and (3, 9). It is translated 2 units left and 4 units down. What are the new coordinates of the vertex at (8, 9)?
items.e: Left 2 changes x: 8 − 2 = 6. Down 4 changes y: 9 − 4 = 5. The new point is (6, 5). Every vertex moves the same way.

items.q: A triangle has vertices at (2, 1), (5, 1), (2, 3). It is translated 3 units right and 4 units up. Which list shows the new vertices?
items.e: Add 3 to every x-coordinate and 4 to every y-coordinate: (2, 1) → (5, 5), (5, 1) → (8, 5), (2, 3) → (5, 7). Move every vertex, not just one.

items.q: Point B is translated 4 units right and 3 units up. It lands on (6, 8). Where did it start?
items.e: Work backwards and undo each move. 4 right is undone by 4 left: 6 − 4 = 2. 3 up is undone by 3 down: 8 − 3 = 5. B started at (2, 5).

items.q: Owen translates (6, 4) 2 units left and gets (8, 4). What mistake did he make?
items.e: Moving left makes the x-coordinate smaller: 6 − 2 = 4. The correct answer is (4, 4). Owen added 2, which is a move to the right.

items.q: A point is translated up or down. Which coordinate changes?
items.e: Up and down is the y direction. The point does not move across, so the x-coordinate stays the same.

items.q: Reflect the point (3, 4) in the vertical line x = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (3, 4) is 2 units to the left of the line x = 5. The image is 2 units to the right of it: 5 + 2 = 7. y stays 4. The image is (7, 4).

items.q: Reflect the point (8, 2) in the vertical line x = 6. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (8, 2) is 2 units to the right of the line x = 6. The image is 2 units to the left of it: 6 − 2 = 4. y stays 2. The image is (4, 2).

items.q: Reflect the point (2, 1) in the horizontal line y = 3. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (2, 1) is 2 units below the line y = 3. The image is 2 units above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 2. The image is (2, 5).

items.q: Reflect the point (6, 9) in the horizontal line y = 6. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (6, 9) is 3 units above the line y = 6. The image is 3 units below it: 6 − 3 = 3. x stays 6. The image is (6, 3).

items.q: Reflect the point (1, 7) in the vertical line x = 4. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (1, 7) is 3 units to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 3 units to the right of it: 4 + 3 = 7. y stays 7. The image is (7, 7).

items.q: Reflect the point (5, 3) in the horizontal line y = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (5, 3) is 2 units below the line y = 5. The image is 2 units above it: 5 + 2 = 7. x stays 5. The image is (5, 7).

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the line x = 4?
items.e: P (2, 3) is 2 units to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 2 units to the right of it: 4 + 2 = 6. y stays 3. The image is (6, 3). That is point B. Point A: it is 1 unit too far (the grid lines were counted, starting with 1 on P’s line). Point C: it stops on the line of reflection. Point D: it was flipped up or down, not across the line.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the line x = 5?
items.e: P (7, 5) is 2 units to the right of the line x = 5. The image is 2 units to the left of it: 5 − 2 = 3. y stays 5. The image is (3, 5). That is point A. Point B: it is 1 unit too far (the grid lines were counted, starting with 1 on P’s line). Point C: it stops on the line of reflection. Point D: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the line y = 3?
items.e: P (3, 1) is 2 units below the line y = 3. The image is 2 units above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 3. The image is (3, 5). That is point D. Point A: it is 1 unit too far (the grid lines were counted, starting with 1 on P’s line). Point B: it stops on the line of reflection. Point C: x and y are swapped.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the line y = 4?
items.e: P (5, 6) is 2 units above the line y = 4. The image is 2 units below it: 4 − 2 = 2. x stays 5. The image is (5, 2). That is point C. Point A: it is 1 unit too far (the grid lines were counted, starting with 1 on P’s line). Point B: it stops on the line of reflection. Point D: it was flipped across, not up or down over the line.

items.q: The green shape is reflected in the dashed line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each vertex of the image must be the same distance from the line as its partner, on the other side. Only D is a true mirror image. Others: A: the shape was flipped upside down, not across the line; B: the shape was slid across, not flipped (it faces the same way); C: the image is 1 unit too far from the line.

items.q: The green shape is reflected in the dashed line. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: Each vertex of the image must be the same distance from the line as its partner, on the other side. Only C is a true mirror image. Others: A: the shape was flipped left to right, not over the line; B: the image is 1 unit too far from the line; D: the shape was slid across, not flipped (it faces the same way).

items.q: Reflect the point (5, 3) in the vertical line x = 5. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: The point (5, 3) is on the line of reflection x = 5, so it does not move: (5, 3). A point on the line of reflection is its own image.

items.q: A point is reflected in a horizontal line. Which coordinate changes?
items.e: A horizontal line goes across. The point flips up or down over it, so only y changes. x stays the same.

items.q: Point P is 3 units to the left of a vertical line of reflection. Where is its image?
c: 3 units to the left of the line
6 units to the right of the line
3 units to the right of the line
4 units to the right of the line
items.e: In a reflection the image is the same distance from the line as the point, on the other side.

items.q: The point (4, 2) is reflected in the horizontal line y = 5. How many units apart are the point and its image?
items.e: (4, 2) is 3 units below y = 5, so the image (4, 8) is 3 units above it. From the point to the image is 3 + 3 = 6 units. (3 is only the distance to the line.)

items.q: The points (2, 6) and (8, 6) are reflections of each other. Where is the line of reflection?
items.e: The line is halfway between the points. From 2 to 8 is 6 units, and half of 6 is 3. 2 + 3 = 5, so the line is x = 5. (y = 6 goes through both points; it is not between them.)

items.q: Olivia wants to reflect shape A in the dashed line. Is shape B correct?
c: No, it is too far from the line
No, it was slid, not flipped
items.e: (1, 1) is 3 units below the line y = 4, so its image should be 3 units above, at (1, 7). B has that vertex at (1, 8): 1 unit too far.

items.q: Emma reflects a right triangle in a vertical line. Her image points the same way as the triangle. What mistake did she make?
c: She slid it instead of flipping it
items.e: A reflection is a mirror image, so it faces the other way. If the image points the same way, the shape was slid (translated).

items.q: A rectangle has vertices at (1, 2), (3, 2), (3, 5), (1, 5). It is reflected in the vertical line x = 4. What are the new coordinates of the vertex at (1, 5)?
items.e: The vertex (1, 5) is 3 units to the left of the line x = 4. The image is 3 units to the right of it: 4 + 3 = 7. y stays 5. The image is (7, 5).

sets.title: Rotations of 90° and 180° about a vertex

items.q: How many degrees is a quarter turn?
items.e: A full turn is 360°. A quarter turn is one of 4 equal parts: 360° ÷ 4 = 90°. A half turn is 180°.

items.q: Which way do the hands of a clock turn?
items.e: Clock hands go from 12 to 3 to 6 to 9: that is clockwise. The other way is counterclockwise.

items.q: A triangle is rotated about its vertex A. Which point stays in the same place?
items.e: The centre of rotation does not move. Here the centre is vertex A; every other point turns around it.

items.q: A shape is rotated 180° clockwise about a point. A copy of it is rotated 180° counterclockwise about the same point. Where do they land?
c: one is a mirror image of the other
one lands twice as far away
items.e: A half turn is a half turn, whichever way you go. 180° clockwise and 180° counterclockwise end in the same place.

items.q: Rotate the point B (6, 4) 90° clockwise about the point A (3, 4). Where does B land?
items.e: From A (3, 4), B (6, 4) is 3 right. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (3, 4), the image is 3 down: (3, 1).

items.q: A triangle has vertices A (4, 4), B (4, 7) and C (6, 4). It is rotated 90° clockwise about vertex A. Where does vertex B land?
items.e: From vertex A (4, 4), vertex B (4, 7) is 3 up. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (4, 4), the image is 3 right: (7, 4).

items.q: Rotate the point Q (8, 5) 90° counterclockwise about the point P (5, 5). Where does Q land?
items.e: From P (5, 5), Q (8, 5) is 3 right. In a 90° counterclockwise turn, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So from (5, 5), the image is 3 up: (5, 8).

items.q: A rectangle has vertices K (3, 3), L (5, 3), M (5, 6) and N (3, 6). It is rotated 90° clockwise about vertex K. Where does vertex M land?
items.e: From vertex K (3, 3), vertex M (5, 6) is 2 right and 3 up. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (3, 3), the image is 3 right and 2 down: (6, 1).

items.q: A triangle has vertices D (5, 3), E (2, 4) and F (5, 6). It is rotated 90° counterclockwise about vertex D. Where does vertex E land?
items.e: From vertex D (5, 3), vertex E (2, 4) is 3 left and 1 up. In a 90° counterclockwise turn, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So from (5, 3), the image is 1 left and 3 down: (4, 0).

items.q: Rotate the point S (8, 5) 180° about the point R (6, 4). Where does S land?
items.e: From R (6, 4), S (8, 5) is 2 right and 1 up. In a 180° turn, right turns into left, left into right, up into down and down into up. So from (6, 4), the image is 2 left and 1 down: (4, 3).

items.q: A triangle has vertices A (4, 4), B (1, 5) and C (4, 7). It is rotated 180° about vertex A. Where does vertex B land?
items.e: From vertex A (4, 4), vertex B (1, 5) is 3 left and 1 up. In a 180° turn, right turns into left, left into right, up into down and down into up. So from (4, 4), the image is 3 right and 1 down: (7, 3).

items.q: The green shape is rotated 90° clockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going right turns to go down in a 90° clockwise turn. Only A shows that. Others: B: a 180° turn; C: a flip (reflection), not a turn; D: a 90° counterclockwise turn.

items.q: The green shape is rotated 90° counterclockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going right turns to go up in a 90° counterclockwise turn. Only D shows that. Others: A: a 180° turn; B: a 90° clockwise turn; C: a flip (reflection), not a turn.

items.q: The green shape is rotated 180° about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going right turns to go left in a 180° turn. Only C shows that. Others: A: a 90° clockwise turn; B: a 90° counterclockwise turn; D: a flip (reflection), not a turn.

items.q: The green shape is rotated 90° clockwise about the red dot. In which picture is the blue image correct?
items.e: The red dot does not move. Follow one side: the side from the red dot going up turns to go right in a 90° clockwise turn. Only B shows that. Others: A: a 180° turn; C: a flip (reflection), not a turn; D: a 90° counterclockwise turn.

items.q: Point P is rotated 90° clockwise about point R. Which point is the image?
items.e: From R (4, 3), P (7, 5) is 3 right and 2 up. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (4, 3), the image is 2 right and 3 down: (6, 0). That is point D. Point A: turned the wrong way (90° counterclockwise). Point B: a 180° turn, not 90°. Point C: the numbers were swapped, but the directions were not turned.

items.q: Point P is rotated 180° about point R. Which point is the image?
items.e: From R (5, 4), P (3, 7) is 2 left and 3 up. In a 180° turn, right turns into left, left into right, up into down and down into up. So from (5, 4), the image is 2 right and 3 down: (7, 1). That is point B. Point A: a 90° turn clockwise, not 180°. Point C: a 90° turn counterclockwise, not 180°. Point D: the numbers were swapped, but the directions were not turned.

items.q: A shape is rotated about the vertex (4, 4). Another vertex moves from (6, 4) to (4, 2). Describe the rotation.
items.e: (6, 4) is 2 right from the centre. (4, 2) is 2 down from the centre. Right turned into down: that is a quarter turn clockwise.

items.q: A shape is rotated about the vertex (3, 3). Another vertex moves from (5, 4) to (1, 2). Describe the rotation.
items.e: (5, 4) is 2 right and 1 up from the centre. (1, 2) is 2 left and 1 down from the centre. Right turned into left and up turned into down: that is a half turn, 180°.

items.q: Amira rotates the point (7, 3) 90° clockwise about (4, 3) and gets (4, 6). What mistake did she make?
items.e: (4, 6) is a quarter turn counterclockwise. From the centre (4, 3), the point (7, 3) is 3 right. In a 90° clockwise turn, right turns into down, down into left, left into up and up into right. So from (4, 3), the image is 3 down: (4, 0).

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B faces the same way as A and is the same size. Every vertex moved 5 units right and 3 units up, for example (1, 1) → (6, 4). That is a translation.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B is a mirror image of A: the foot of the L points the other way. It is a reflection in the line x = 5. The size has not changed.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: In A the long arm of the L lies flat along the bottom. In B it stands straight up. A slide or a flip cannot make a flat arm stand up, but a turn can: B is A turned 90° clockwise about the vertex (5, 5).

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: B is A turned upside down and back to front: a half turn (180°) about the vertex (5, 2). A single flip would change only one of these.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: In A the right angle is at the bottom left; in B it is at the top left. B is A flipped over the line y = 4: each vertex is the same distance from the line on the other side, for example (2, 5) → (2, 3). That is a reflection.

items.q: What happened to shape A to make shape B?
items.e: A is 4 units by 2 units. B is only 2 units by 1 unit, so B is smaller. A translation, a reflection or a rotation never changes the size.

items.q: In a coding lesson, Ethan’s robot starts at (1, 2). The code says: move 4 right, then move 3 up. Where does the robot stop?
items.e: Right 4 changes x: 1 + 4 = 5. Up 3 changes y: 2 + 3 = 5. The new point is (5, 5).

items.q: Aiden’s robot is at (2, 7). He wants it to stop at (6, 3). Which code works?
items.e: The start is at (2, 7) and the end is at (6, 3). Across: 2 to 6 is 4 units right. Up and down: 7 to 3 is 4 units down. Count the spaces you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: In a board game, each turn moves a counter 2 units right. Zoe’s counter starts at (1, 4). Where is it after 3 turns?
items.e: 3 turns is 3 × 2 = 6 units right. x: 1 + 6 = 7. y stays 4. The counter is at (7, 4).

items.q: On a map of a campsite, the fire pit is at (3, 5) and the canoe dock is at (8, 1). Describe the translation from the fire pit to the dock.
items.e: The fire pit is at (3, 5) and the dock is at (8, 1). Across: 3 to 8 is 5 units right. Up and down: 5 to 1 is 4 units down. Count the spaces you jump, not the lines you touch.

items.q: On a hockey play diagram, Arjun skates from (2, 3), 6 units right and 4 units up. Where does he stop?
items.e: Right 6 changes x: 2 + 6 = 8. Up 4 changes y: 3 + 4 = 7. The new point is (8, 7).

items.q: Sofia makes a paper snowflake design for the class window. The design is symmetrical in the line x = 5. One tip is at (2, 6). Where is the matching tip?
items.e: The tip (2, 6) is 3 units to the left of the line x = 5. The image is 3 units to the right of it: 5 + 3 = 8. y stays 6. The image is (8, 6).

items.q: A school crest is symmetrical in the horizontal line y = 5. One corner is at (3, 2). Where is the matching corner?
items.e: The corner (3, 2) is 3 units below the line y = 5. The image is 3 units above it: 5 + 3 = 8. x stays 3. The image is (3, 8).

items.q: A garden has a path along the line x = 5. A flower bed with vertices at (1, 2), (3, 2), (3, 4), (1, 4) is reflected in the path to make a matching bed. Which list shows the vertices of the new bed?
items.e: Each vertex goes the same distance on the other side of x = 5: (1, 2) is 4 units left, so its image is 4 units right, at (9, 2). (3, 2) is 2 units left, so its image is (7, 2).

items.q: Nathan draws a pinwheel for a Terry Fox Run poster. One blade tip is at (7, 6). The next blade is the first one rotated 90° counterclockwise about the centre (5, 5). Where is the next tip?
items.e: From the centre (5, 5), the tip (7, 6) is 2 right and 1 up. In a 90° counterclockwise turn, right turns into up, up into left, left into down and down into right. So from (5, 5), the image is 1 left and 2 up: (4, 7).

items.q: Benjamin makes a quilt pattern. A triangle has a vertex at (8, 7). He rotates the triangle 180° about its vertex (6, 6). Where does the vertex at (8, 7) go?
items.e: From the centre (6, 6), the vertex (8, 7) is 2 right and 1 up. In a 180° turn, right turns into left, left into right, up into down and down into up. So from (6, 6), the image is 2 left and 1 down: (4, 5).

items.q: Hana turns a puzzle piece about its corner at (4, 4). Another corner moves from (6, 4) to (4, 6). How did she turn it?
items.e: (6, 4) is 2 right of the centre. (4, 6) is 2 up from the centre. Right turned into up: that is a quarter turn counterclockwise.

items.q: In a game, a counter at (7, 3) is reflected in the horizontal line y = 4, then translated 2 units left. Where does it end?
items.e: Reflect first: (7, 3) is 1 unit below y = 4, so the image is 1 unit above, at (7, 5). Then left 2: 7 − 2 = 5. It ends at (5, 5).

items.q: A rug on a floor plan covers 6 squares. It is rotated 90° about one corner. Which sentence is true?
items.e: A rotation turns the rug but does not stretch it. The side lengths, angles and area stay the same, so it still covers 6 squares.

items.q: Which move makes a mirror image of a shape?
items.e: A reflection flips the shape over a line, so the image faces the other way like in a mirror. A translation slides the shape and a rotation turns it; neither flips it.
